summary: MISSION ZERO is a 3D space-simulation game for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 that makes the player commander of a mission. It has two connected phases. In Space Journey, players manage the spacecraft and monitor oxygen, food, water, air quality, power, temperature, humidity, pressure, and radiation while handling emergencies power failures, air leaks, recycling failures, and solar storms. In Colony Survival, they build a lunar or Martian base with habitats, power, water, food, oxygen, greenhouses, and maintenance. Journey decisions affect colonization: low supplies, damaged equipment, or crew losses make survival harder. The project uses NASA open data—ECLSS, NASA-STD-3001, POWER, and lunar/Mars datasets—converted into simplified gameplay equations. Built with Unity 6, C#, and Blender, it features dynamic events, trade-offs, and six-person team covering development, 3D design, UI/UX, mission design, research, QA, and presentation. Goal: entertaining, scientifically grounded learning about resource management and systems thinking beyond Earth. Build Beyond Earth.
details:
MISSION ZERO – Build Beyond Earth

MISSION ZERO is an interactive 3D space-survival simulation that explores the challenges astronauts may face during a journey to Mars. The player takes the role of a crew member responsible for monitoring and maintaining the spacecraft's life-support systems.

The simulation focuses on essential resources and environmental conditions, including oxygen, carbon dioxide, water, food, electrical power, cabin pressure, and temperature. These systems are interconnected, so a failure in one system can affect the entire crew and spacecraft.

As the mission progresses, unexpected equipment failures and system problems can occur. Players must monitor the spacecraft's indicators, identify problems, and respond by activating the appropriate repair or recovery actions. Their decisions influence resource availability and the crew's ability to continue the journey safely.

The project is being developed using Unity and C#. The team uses 3D environments, interactive user interfaces, gameplay systems, and a time-based simulation model to make complex space-survival concepts understandable and engaging.

Our goal is to create an educational experience that encourages systems thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and awareness of the challenges involved in human space exploration. MISSION ZERO is an educational simulation inspired by real spaceflight life-support concepts; it is not intended to be an exact engineering replica of an operational spacecraft.
